description:
crate-jmap-sharing-server/src/backend.rs:69-75

```rust
/// Destroy a Principal or ShareNotification by id.
fn destroy_object<O: SetObject + Send + Sync>(
    &self,
    caller: &Self::CallerCtx,
    account_id: &jmap_types::Id,
    id: &jmap_types::Id,
) -> impl std::future::Future<Output = Result<(), BackendSetError<Self::Error>>> + Send;
```

The entire contract documentation for destroy is a single sentence:
\"Destroy a Principal or ShareNotification by id.\"

A backend implementor reading this has no answer to any of:

1. **What if `id` does not exist?** Must return
   `BackendSetError::SetError(SetError::new(SetErrorType::NotFound))`
   per RFC 8620 §5.3, but the trait does not say so. The handler at
   `notification.rs:121-148` maps the SetError variants verbatim
   into the wire response, so getting the wrong variant produces an
   incorrect JMAP response that no Rust-level test would catch.

2. **What if `id` exists but the caller lacks permission?** Must
   return `SetErrorType::Forbidden`. Documented nowhere. The crate's
   AGENTS.md says backend is canonical for permission enforcement,
   but that AGENTS.md note is not part of the public API contract
   that a third-party SharingBackend implementor reads.

3. **What if `account_id` does not exist?** Tied to JMAP-3t94.1 and
   JMAP-3t94.2 — but the trait should explicitly say the backend may
   assume `account_exists` was verified by the handler (which is
   currently NOT TRUE per .1), or that the backend must verify it
   itself.

4. **What are the state-mutation guarantees?** Should the backend
   bump its state counter only if the destroy succeeds? Should it
   record a change-log entry? Should the change-log entry be
   atomic with the destroy? None of this is in the trait doc; the
   MemoryBackend impl (`memory.rs:576-605`) shows the workspace
   answer but a downstream impl cannot rely on undocumented
   pattern-by-example.

5. **Idempotency on already-destroyed.** If the caller destroys
   the same id twice, does the second call return `Ok(())` or
   `Err(NotFound)`? MemoryBackend returns `Err(NotFound)`. RFC 8620
   §5.3 doesn't strictly require either.

What goes wrong for callers when this stays as-is: backend
implementors guess the contract differently. Cross-backend
behavior diverges. JMAP clients written against one backend see
different error wire-shapes against another. The handler's
mapping of SetError to wire response is the only test coverage,
and that test only catches the variants the existing MemoryBackend
happens to produce.

Resolution: enumerate the canonical SetErrorType variants per
condition (NotFound, Forbidden, ifInState mismatch). Cite RFC 8620
§5.3. State the state-mutation contract.
notes: Expanded SharingBackend::destroy_object rustdoc with full error contract (NotFound for missing id, Forbidden for permission, accountNotFound handler-vs-backend layering, Other for storage failures), state-mutation contract (state advances only on commit, change-log entry atomic with state advance), and idempotency (second destroy is NotFound — workspace convention shared with canonical jmap-mail-server).
title: SharingBackend::destroy_object — one-line docstring; no error contract, no SetErrorType guidance, no state-mutation contract
